title: Best Portrait Photographers (2026): Headshots and Personal Portraits
description: How to hire a portrait photographer for headshots, personal branding or family portraits: style, editing, rights, how to brief it, price drivers and red flags.
intro: Portrait photographers capture people: professional headshots, personal branding photos, family portraits, actor and model portfolios and creative portraits. A good portrait looks natural, flattering and true to the person. Sessions go wrong when the style is not agreed, the person feels uncomfortable in front of the camera, or editing is heavier than expected. This guide helps you get portraits you are happy to use.

faq.a: Simple, well-fitting clothes in colors that suit you and your brand. Bring a change or two. Avoid busy patterns unless they fit the style.

faq.q: How many photos will I get?
faq.a: Agree on the number of edited images and whether you can choose from proofs.
Usually color correction and light retouching. Heavy retouching should be discussed and kept natural.

faq.q: Can I use the photos for business?
faq.a: Agree on usage rights, especially for advertising, book covers or press.

faq.q: Can a photographer edit photos I already have?
faq.a: Some portrait photographers also offer remote retouching of your own photos.
